obligation: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard, as a service provider (Visa Level 1)
citation: PCI DSS v4.0.1; card brand rules through the sponsor agreements
basis: The company stores, processes and transmits cardholder data for its merchants and ISV partners, and both sponsor agreements require PCI DSS compliance. At about 820 million transactions a year it is a Level 1 service provider under Visa's published levels (more than 300,000 a year). Both banks accept one combined 2026 AOC by 2026-12-15

obligation: PCI PIN Security Requirements
basis: The company does not acquire PIN-based debit transactions and holds no PIN keys; merchants that need PIN debit are referred to a partner processor

obligation: FTC Standards for Safeguarding Customer Information (Safeguards Rule)
basis: A non-bank financial institution under FTC jurisdiction: data processing of financial data is listed in 12 CFR 225.28(b)(14) and is financial in nature under 12 U.S.C. 1843(k) (314.1(b); 314.2(h)(1)). It holds customer information of other financial institutions' customers (cardholders) (314.1(b)). Not eligible for the 314.6 exception (data on millions of cardholders). It has a board, so the Qualified Individual reports to the board (314.4(i))

obligation: Computer-Security Incident Notification Rule: bank service provider notice to Bank A (OCC)
basis: Bank A is a national bank. Its sponsor agreement names clearing, settlement, reconciliation and merchant funding file services as subject to examination under 12 U.S.C. 1867(c), so they are covered services and the company is a bank service provider (53.1(c); 53.2(b)(2), (b)(5)). No size threshold

obligation: Computer-Security Incident Notification Rule: bank service provider notice to Bank B (FDIC)
basis: Bank B is an FDIC-supervised insured state nonmember bank, and its sponsor agreement (in effect 2025-10-01) has the same 1867(c) clause (304.21(c); 304.22(b)(2), (b)(5))

obligation: Computer-Security Incident Notification Rule: Federal Reserve bank service provider notice
basis: The company performs no services for a Board-supervised banking organization (225.300(c); 225.301(b)(1)); its bank customers are the two sponsor banks

obligation: Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards
citation: 12 CFR 30 App. B (OCC); 12 CFR 364 App. B (FDIC)
applies: No (binds the sponsor banks; reaches the company through the sponsor agreements)
basis: The Guidelines apply to the banks. They reach the company only through the sponsor agreements' service provider, security and audit terms, which both banks test in annual due diligence

obligation: NCUA cyber incident reporting
basis: The company is not a credit union and serves none

obligation: SEC Regulation SCI
basis: Not an SCI entity; the company is privately held and not an SEC registrant, so SEC cyber disclosure rules do not apply either

obligation: NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation
basis: The regulation applies to entities licensed, registered or chartered under New York banking, insurance or financial services law; the company holds no New York license, registration or charter

obligation: CIRCIA (pending rule)
basis: No final rule; tracked for planning. If finalized as proposed, the company would likely be covered because its receipts exceed the SBA size standard for NAICS 522320

obligation: Bank Service Company Act examination of services performed for the banks
basis: Both sponsor agreements state that the clearing, settlement, reconciliation and merchant funding file services are subject to examination by the banks' regulators

obligation: Card brand incident rules (Visa What To Do If Compromised and other brands' rules)
citation: Visa Core Rules and supplements; other brands' rules through the sponsor banks
basis: The sponsor banks registered the company with the card brands as their third-party processor

obligation: Sponsor agreement terms: file cutoffs and 24-hour notice of suspected account data compromise
basis: Each agreement requires clearing and funding files by the bank's daily cutoff and notice to the bank of any suspected account data compromise within 24 hours

obligation: Merchant and ISV partner agreements: 99.95% availability
citation: Merchant agreement and ISV partner agreement templates
basis: Merchant agreements promise 99.95% monthly availability for authorization; ISV agreements promise 99.95% for the Integrated Payments API

obligation: Requests for a SOC 2 Type 2 report
citation: Sponsor bank due diligence requests; ISV partner requests
basis: Both sponsor banks asked in their 2026 due diligence, and the 5 largest ISV partners have asked

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (breach notification and data security)
basis: The company holds personal information of Florida residents: for cardholder data it is usually a third-party agent of its merchants (501.171(6)); for merchant owner data it is a covered entity

obligation: Breach notification laws of other states
citation: Each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Merchants are located in all 50 states, so each affected person's state law applies; counsel applies them during an incident

obligation: FTC Act Section 5 (unfair or deceptive practices)
basis: Applies to the company's claims to merchants and to practices affecting consumers, including AI-driven declines and chatbot statements

obligation: Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Regulation B for merchant scoring (AI-002)
applies: Not determined (to be confirmed by counsel)
basis: Whether merchant processing approval and reserves are credit under ECOA was not determined at intake

obligation: State automated decision-making laws (Colorado SB26-189, effective 2027-01-01; California ADMT rules)
applies: Not determined (to be assessed by counsel)
basis: Merchants and cardholders are in all 50 states and AI-001 and AI-002 affect individuals; applicability was not assessed at intake

obligation: State money transmission licensing
basis: Merchant funds settle through the sponsor banks' accounts
